project.title: Economic case and governance design for a national agricultural sustainability framework
project.quote: Australia has a small window of opportunity to lead the world on sustainability communication.
project.summary: The Australian Farm Institute engaged Heuris to build the economic rationale and governance design for the Australian Agricultural Sustainability Framework, a Commonwealth-funded initiative to give Australian agriculture a common sustainability language. The framework had objectives but no articulated problem definition. We established the gap in economic terms — an information failure across a fragmented certification landscape — then designed a governance structure to close it, stress-tested against international precedent.
points: Defined the framework's rationale as an information failure, giving the program a testable problem statement it previously lacked
Mapped the sustainability landscape into drivers, facilitators, metrics and assessment programs — the classification the framework now rests on
Applied the Regulator–Intermediary–Target model to position the framework as a domestic translation layer for global standards
Designed a four-part governance structure: Translation and Communications Group, industry Technical Working Groups, Markets and Information Group, and Board
Identified independence from both industry capture and government regulation as the precondition for the framework's legitimacy
Set out international recognition pathways, including ISEAL standards-holder membership and mutual mapping to existing frameworks

metrics.label: Structured review reports plus a synthesis, forming the framework's evidence base
Governance components designed, from technical working groups through to board
International governance case studies used to stress-test the design
Competing Australian sustainability schemes mapped in the underpinning review

steps.label: PROBLEM DEFINITION
steps.title: Named the market failure the framework exists to correct
steps.text: A rationale was missing from the program documentation, leaving objectives untethered. We defined the gap as information failure — producers unable to identify which schemes meet which market requirements, at costs that deter participation entirely.

steps.label: ECONOMIC FOUNDATIONS
steps.title: Why sustainability claims fail without credible assurance
steps.text: Environmental production claims are strong credence attributes: unverifiable by testing the product. We showed how the resulting asymmetry produces both green-washing and gold-plating, and why neither resolves without an intermediary.

steps.label: GOVERNANCE DESIGN
steps.title: A translation layer between global frameworks and Australian industry
steps.text: Using the Regulator–Intermediary–Target model, we designed a structure positioning the framework as an accredited domestic translation of international standards — with independence from industry capture built into the governance, not added afterwards.

steps.label: STRESS-TESTING
steps.title: Tested the design against precedent and failure
steps.text: Benchmarked the proposed structure against GLOBALG.A.P.'s governance and against a documented governance failure in Australian construction, then set out test cases and open questions for the program's next phase.
